'''Mysore Ananthamurthy Viswamitra''' (14 November 1932 – 10 April 2001) was an Indian [[Molecular biophysics|molecular biophysicist]] and [[Crystallography|crystallographer]], known for his pioneering work on the [[X-ray]] structural studies of [[DNA|DNA fragments]] and [[nucleotide]] [[coenzyme]] molecules.<ref name="Mysore Ananthamurthy Viswamitra - NeglectedScience">{{Cite web |url=http://www.neglectedscience.com/alphabetical-list/v/mysore-ananthamurthy-viswamitra |title=Mysore Ananthamurthy Viswamitra - NeglectedScience |date=2018-12-18 |website=www.neglectedscience.com |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> His work is reported to have assisted in the development of the concept of sequence-dependent [[Oligonucleotide|oligonucleotide conformation]]. He was an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] senior scientist and an MSIL chair professor of physics at the [[Indian Institute of Science]]<ref name="Endowed chairs for the Faculty">{{Cite web |url=https://www.iisc.ac.in/about/endowed-chairs/endowed-chairs-for-the-faculty/ |title=Endowed chairs for the Faculty |date=2018-12-18 |website=Indian Institute of Science |language=en |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> and a visiting professor at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="INSA - Deceased Fellow Detail">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/detail/N83-0880 |title=INSA - Deceased Fellow Detail |date=2018-12-18 |website=www.insaindia.res.in |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born on 14 November 1932, in [[Shimoga]], in the south Indian state of [[Karnataka]], Viswamitra did his early education at the [[University of Mysore]] and [[Banaras Hindu University]] before securing a PhD from the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc) and joined IISc in 1954.<ref name="The Hindu : Scientist dies after addressing condolence meet">{{Cite web |url=https://www.thehindu.com/thehindu/2001/04/11/stories/0411402j.htm |title=Scientist dies after addressing condolence meet |date=11 April 2001 |website=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=2018-12-18}}{{dead link|date=September 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He served IISc till his superannuation in 1993 during which time he founded the School of Biocrystallography and the Bioinformatics Centre at the institution. He is reported to have determined the structure of a number of [[Nucleotide|mononucleotides]] for the first time and, along with [[Olga Kennard]], elucidated the [[oligonucleotide]] dp(AT)2 structure leading to the first atomic detail view of a DNA duplex.<ref name="Mysore Ananthamurthy Viswamitra - NeglectedScience" /> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles has listed 141 of them.<ref name="M. A. Viswamitra's research works - Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, Bengaluru (JNCASR) and other places">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/55808058_M_A_Viswamitra |title=M. A. Viswamitra's research works - Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, Bengaluru (JNCASR) and other places |date=2018-12-18 |website=ResearchGate |language=en |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref>

Viswamitra was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies viz. the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Viswamitra,_Prof._Mysore_Ananthamurthy |title=Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2018-12-18 |website=www.ias.ac.in |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> the [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name="The Hindu : Scientist dies after addressing condolence meet" /> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="The National Academy of Sciences, India Deceased Fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |title=The National Academy of Sciences, India Deceased Fellows |date=2018-12-18 |website=www.nasi.org.in |access-date=2018-12-18 |archive-date=28 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528102550/http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> as well as the [[World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS).<ref name="TWAS Fellow">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/directory/viswamitra-mysore-ananthamurty |title=TWAS Fellow |date=2018-12-18 |website=TWAS |language=en-US |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> He was a recipient of a number of awards which included C. V. Raman Award of the Acoustical Society of India (1982),<ref name="SIR C V RAMAN AWARD">{{Cite web |url=http://acoustics.org.in/?page_id=132 |title=SIR C V RAMAN AWARD |date=2018-03-14 |website=Acoustical Society of India |language=en-US |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> J. C. Bose Award of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] (1984), [[TWAS Prize]] (1986), J. C. Bose Medal of the [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] (1986), R.D. Birla National Award (1988), [[Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry|FICCI]] Award (1991), S. S. Bhatnagar Medal of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (1993), National Citizens Award (1998) and the Distinguished Alumni Award of the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (1999).<ref name="INSA - Deceased Fellow Detail" />

Viswamitra died, succumbing to a heart attack, on 10 April 2001, at the age of 68, survived by his wife and son. The death occurred immediately after he delivered a public speech at the condolence meeting of his colleague, [[G. N. Ramachandran]].<ref name="The Hindu : Scientist dies after addressing condolence meet" />
